guides.title: Quick Start: build a useful first day
guides.summary: An eight-step, resumable setup for people, opening balances, equipment, stock and first work. Works on phone and computer.
guides.example: A Super starts with confirmed data and a real first assignment.
guides.pitfall: Do not invent readings, quantities or prior spending. Review before publishing; release email separately.

steps.title: Confirm your operation
steps.text: Open Quick Start from My Day or More. Confirm the property address and current track. An unavailable track is not activated. Existing forecast points and source maps are preserved.
steps.example: Kings Course now; Ridge stays deferred.

steps.title: Decide what is shared
steps.text: Review each resource separately: crew, budget, Garage, pumps, chemicals, parts, fuel, seed and facilities. Matching groups share a canonical record; separate groups keep separate records. Another manager’s tracks require their approval. The current live release activates single-track properties; multi-track migration requires coordinated support.
steps.example: One shed and one budget; equipment sharing is a separate choice.

steps.title: Start from a known balance
steps.text: Check I know the remaining budget balance, enter the amount, as-of date and end date. Say whether recorded commitments were already deducted. Leave the choice off to keep your existing budget. Review blocks an overlapping new budget rather than overwriting it.
steps.example: $48,000 remaining as of today; no historic spending invented.

steps.title: Add people and working hours
steps.text: Choose a job title, email, language and Crew or Super access separately. Add working days, start/end times and availability dates. A matching verified signed-in email links your own crew profile. Review fails if first assignments are outside recorded hours.
steps.example: Spray Technician with Crew access, Monday–Friday 06:00–14:00.

steps.title: Confirm the equipment baseline
steps.text: Choose a known model or enter custom equipment. Confirm condition, meter type and the current reading. Choose Unknown instead of entering a made-up zero. Catalog browsing creates no inventory or maintenance history.
steps.example: A mower has 1,245 hours today, not a guessed lifetime history.

steps.title: Count what you actually have
steps.text: Add exact chemical references, seed/materials, parts, tanks and maintenance facilities. Confirm quantities only after checking them. Opening balances are not new spending. Unknown parts value must be recorded in Parts before costed issue. Fuel quantity confirmation currently requires a unit cost. Chemical use still needs label/SDS and local review.
steps.example: 12 bags counted today; unknown stock stays unconfirmed.

steps.title: Make the first day useful
steps.text: Assign an existing or new worker, a date, time, duration, clear instructions and optional Garage equipment. Classify Planned or Emergency. Review checks crew hours, bookings, equipment condition and event restrictions. Choose My Day after publishing, or Team today to review others’ work.
steps.example: An operating mower and qualified worker, booked before play.

steps.title: Review, publish and release separately
steps.text: Select Check setup before publishing. Correct any error, review the counts and confirm Publish reviewed setup. The starting state is saved and read back before publication. Work and welcome emails stay held. Release them only after reviewing the people and assignments. Save & exit keeps an unfinished draft. Demo changes expire and never send real emails.
steps.example: Draft → review → publish → release messages → My Day.

es.title: Inicio rápido: prepare el primer día
es.summary: Configure personas, saldos, equipos, existencias y primeras tareas en ocho pasos. Funciona en teléfono y computadora.

steps.title: Confirme su operación
steps.text: Abra Inicio rápido desde Mi día o Más. Confirme la dirección y el recorrido actual. No se activa un recorrido no disponible ni se modifica el mapa.
steps.example: Kings Course now; Ridge stays deferred.

steps.title: Decida qué se comparte
steps.text: Revise personal, presupuesto, equipos, bombas, productos, repuestos, combustible, semillas e instalaciones por separado. Los grupos comunes comparten un registro. La activación de varias pistas requiere una migración coordinada.
steps.example: One shed and one budget; equipment sharing is a separate choice.

steps.title: Comience con un saldo conocido
steps.text: Indique el saldo restante, la fecha y el fin del período. Aclare si ya se descontaron compromisos registrados. Puede conservar el presupuesto actual; no se inventan gastos anteriores.
steps.example: $48,000 remaining as of today; no historic spending invented.

steps.title: Añada personas y horarios
steps.text: Elija cargo, correo, idioma y acceso Personal o Super por separado. Registre días, horas y fechas. El correo verificado de su cuenta vincula su propio perfil. Las primeras tareas deben respetar las horas registradas.
steps.example: Spray Technician with Crew access, Monday–Friday 06:00–14:00.

steps.title: Confirme la base de los equipos
steps.text: Elija un modelo o añada su equipo. Confirme estado, medidor y lectura actual. Elija Desconocido cuando corresponda. Explorar el catálogo no crea historial.
steps.example: A mower has 1,245 hours today, not a guessed lifetime history.

steps.title: Cuente lo que realmente tiene
steps.text: Añada productos, semillas, materiales, repuestos, tanques e instalaciones. Confirme cantidades medidas. Los saldos iniciales no son gastos nuevos. Registre el valor de repuestos antes de emitirlos con costo; el combustible inicial requiere costo unitario.
steps.example: 12 bags counted today; unknown stock stays unconfirmed.

steps.title: Prepare el primer día
steps.text: Asigne persona, fecha, hora, duración, instrucciones y equipo opcional. Clasifique trabajo Planificado o Emergencia. Se revisan horarios, reservas, estado del equipo y restricciones de eventos.
steps.example: An operating mower and qualified worker, booked before play.

steps.title: Revise, publique y envíe por separado
steps.text: Compruebe la configuración, corrija errores y confirme la publicación. Se conserva una copia inicial verificada. Los correos quedan retenidos hasta que los libere. Guardar y salir conserva el borrador. La demostración no envía correos reales.
steps.example: Draft → review → publish → release messages → My Day.

classes.deviceNote: This course teaches the phone field layout: Today, Map, Schedule and More. Some demonstrations require superintendent access; workers use only their assigned tickets. classes.summary: A practical phone-only class: navigate the course, report issues, read work and keep the crew informed.
classes.facilitator: Lead the examples in the fictional demo. Demonstrate manager-only tools from your authorized view. Ask learners to explain each next action before practicing; the class never grants permissions or qualifications.

quiz.question: Where do you find layers on a phone?
quiz.answer: More → Map layers. Close the panel to pan freely.

quiz.question: Does a closure request mean the work order is approved?
quiz.answer: No. A superintendent or authorized assistant must inspect and approve it.

steps.title: Start with four places
steps.text: Today is your own work. Map opens the course. Schedule opens the calendar. More groups the remaining workspaces and help. Managers use Team today or Crew for the team; workers see only their assignments.
steps.example: Name the next tap before starting.

steps.title: Give the map room
steps.text: Choose a hole, close the panel, then drag with one finger and pinch with two to zoom. Use the crosshair to fit the view. More → Map layers reduces clutter without removing records.
steps.example: Open Hole 3 and find the green.

steps.title: Open the feature before editing
steps.text: Tap the exact feature and check its label. The compact strip has Details, Move, Size or Repair as appropriate. Preview every position/size edit and confirm before saving; use More → Map details & undo for a recent mistake.
steps.example: Select a sprinkler without moving it.

steps.title: Make the problem actionable
steps.text: Managers can report a feature repair, choose planned or emergency and link a worker. Workers report through their assigned ticket or the course escalation process. Capture GPS only at the actual issue and check the displayed accuracy; this lesson never activates GPS.
steps.example: Describe symptoms separately from the suspected cause.

steps.title: See the day and resolve timing
steps.text: Open Schedule, choose Day or Week and open a dated job. Tap a move grip if dragging is difficult. A manager reviews worker, equipment and event conflicts before confirming a new date. New phone schedules are one-time work; repeat programs are in Full tools.
steps.example: Move no job until the proposed date is reviewed.

steps.title: Record the work and request closure
steps.text: Open your ticket, read the instructions and log actual work and time when known. Submit for closure asks for inspection; it does not close the ticket. A superintendent or authorized assistant approves or returns it. Read the history to confirm who acted.
steps.control: Record work performed / Submit for closure
steps.example: A repair stays highlighted while approval is pending.

steps.title: Use the field records
steps.text: Managers find Equipment and Pump stations under More → Assets & supplies for readings, condition and repair work. Chemical actual entry has three steps: When & where, Product quantities, Conditions & checks. Use actual reviewed instructions; the demo is not application guidance.
steps.example: Check the machine identity before recording a reading.

steps.title: Check status and keep a way back
steps.text: Budget and Reports under More → Course & insight provide compact manager summaries. Office setup remains behind Full tools; Return to field view switches back. If signal fails, keep and review an offline draft; confirm a successful save and history before treating it as shared.
steps.example: End the walkthrough, then practice in the temporary demo.

quiz.question: ¿Dónde están las capas en el teléfono?
quiz.answer: Más → Capas del mapa. Cierre el panel para mover libremente.

quiz.question: ¿La solicitud de cierre es una aprobación?
quiz.answer: No. El superintendente o asistente autorizado debe revisar y aprobar.

steps.title: Empiece con cuatro lugares
steps.text: Hoy es su trabajo. Mapa abre el campo. Calendario abre la programación. Más agrupa espacios y ayuda. Los responsables usan Equipo hoy o Personal; los trabajadores solo ven sus asignaciones.
steps.example: Diga el siguiente toque antes de empezar.

steps.title: Dé espacio al mapa
steps.text: Elija un hoyo, cierre el panel y arrastre con un dedo; pellizque con dos para ampliar. La mira encuadra la vista. Más → Capas reduce detalle sin borrar registros.
steps.example: Abra el hoyo 3 y busque el green.

steps.title: Abra el elemento antes de editar
steps.text: Pulse el elemento y compruebe su etiqueta. La barra muestra Detalles, Mover, Tamaño o Reparación según corresponda. Revise y confirme cambios antes de guardar; Más → Detalles y deshacer permite corregir un cambio reciente.
steps.example: Seleccione un aspersor sin moverlo.

steps.title: Haga que el problema sea accionable
steps.text: Los responsables notifican reparaciones, eligen planificado o emergencia y enlazan trabajadores. El personal informa desde su orden o el proceso local. Capture GPS solo en el lugar real y compruebe precisión; la lección no activa GPS.
steps.example: Separe síntomas de causas sospechadas.

steps.title: Vea el día y resuelva horarios
steps.text: Abra Calendario, elija Día o Semana y una tarea. Pulse el agarre si arrastrar resulta difícil. El responsable revisa conflictos de personal, equipos y eventos antes de confirmar. Los nuevos horarios del teléfono son únicos; las repeticiones están en Todas las herramientas.
steps.example: No mueva una tarea sin revisar la fecha propuesta.

steps.title: Registre trabajo y solicite cierre
steps.text: Abra su orden, lea instrucciones y registre trabajo y tiempo reales si se conocen. Enviar para cierre pide inspección; no cierra la orden. El superintendente o asistente autorizado aprueba o devuelve. Lea quién actuó en el historial.
steps.example: La reparación sigue resaltada hasta la aprobación.

steps.title: Use los registros de campo
steps.text: Los responsables encuentran Equipos y Estaciones de bombeo en Más → Equipos y suministros para lecturas, estado y reparaciones. El registro químico tiene tres pasos: Cuándo y dónde, Cantidades y Condiciones. Use instrucciones revisadas reales; la demo no indica aplicaciones.
steps.example: Compruebe la máquina antes de registrar lecturas.

steps.title: Revise estado y conserve una salida
steps.text: Presupuesto e Informes en Más → Campo e informes ofrecen resúmenes para responsables. La configuración está en Todas las herramientas; Volver a la vista de campo recupera la vista sencilla. Sin señal conserve y revise un borrador; confirme guardado e historial antes de tratarlo como compartido.
steps.example: Termine el recorrido y practique en la demo temporal.

classes.title: Practice launching an operation
classes.summary: A practical setup class: use the fictional course, confirm baselines, assign first work, and discuss what must stay unknown.
classes.example: A Super starts with confirmed data and a real first assignment.
classes.pitfall: Do not invent readings, quantities or prior spending. Review before publishing; release email separately.

steps.title: Confirm your operation
steps.text: Open Quick Start from My Day or More. Confirm the property address and current track. An unavailable track is not activated. Existing forecast points and source maps are preserved.
steps.example: Kings Course now; Ridge stays deferred.

steps.title: Decide what is shared
steps.text: Review each resource separately: crew, budget, Garage, pumps, chemicals, parts, fuel, seed and facilities. Matching groups share a canonical record; separate groups keep separate records. Another manager’s tracks require their approval. The current live release activates single-track properties; multi-track migration requires coordinated support.
steps.example: One shed and one budget; equipment sharing is a separate choice.

steps.title: Start from a known balance
steps.text: Check I know the remaining budget balance, enter the amount, as-of date and end date. Say whether recorded commitments were already deducted. Leave the choice off to keep your existing budget. Review blocks an overlapping new budget rather than overwriting it.
steps.example: $48,000 remaining as of today; no historic spending invented.

steps.title: Add people and working hours
steps.text: Choose a job title, email, language and Crew or Super access separately. Add working days, start/end times and availability dates. A matching verified signed-in email links your own crew profile. Review fails if first assignments are outside recorded hours.
steps.example: Spray Technician with Crew access, Monday–Friday 06:00–14:00.

steps.title: Confirm the equipment baseline
steps.text: Choose a known model or enter custom equipment. Confirm condition, meter type and the current reading. Choose Unknown instead of entering a made-up zero. Catalog browsing creates no inventory or maintenance history.
steps.example: A mower has 1,245 hours today, not a guessed lifetime history.

steps.title: Count what you actually have
steps.text: Add exact chemical references, seed/materials, parts, tanks and maintenance facilities. Confirm quantities only after checking them. Opening balances are not new spending. Unknown parts value must be recorded in Parts before costed issue. Fuel quantity confirmation currently requires a unit cost. Chemical use still needs label/SDS and local review.
steps.example: 12 bags counted today; unknown stock stays unconfirmed.

steps.title: Make the first day useful
steps.text: Assign an existing or new worker, a date, time, duration, clear instructions and optional Garage equipment. Classify Planned or Emergency. Review checks crew hours, bookings, equipment condition and event restrictions. Choose My Day after publishing, or Team today to review others’ work.
steps.example: An operating mower and qualified worker, booked before play.

steps.title: Review, publish and release separately
steps.text: Select Check setup before publishing. Correct any error, review the counts and confirm Publish reviewed setup. The starting state is saved and read back before publication. Work and welcome emails stay held. Release them only after reviewing the people and assignments. Save & exit keeps an unfinished draft. Demo changes expire and never send real emails.
steps.example: Draft → review → publish → release messages → My Day.

es.title: Practique el inicio de una operación
es.summary: Clase práctica con el campo ficticio: confirme bases, asigne trabajo y conserve datos desconocidos sin inventarlos.

steps.title: Confirme su operación
steps.text: Abra Inicio rápido desde Mi día o Más. Confirme la dirección y el recorrido actual. No se activa un recorrido no disponible ni se modifica el mapa.
steps.example: Kings Course now; Ridge stays deferred.

steps.title: Decida qué se comparte
steps.text: Revise personal, presupuesto, equipos, bombas, productos, repuestos, combustible, semillas e instalaciones por separado. Los grupos comunes comparten un registro. La activación de varias pistas requiere una migración coordinada.
steps.example: One shed and one budget; equipment sharing is a separate choice.

steps.title: Comience con un saldo conocido
steps.text: Indique el saldo restante, la fecha y el fin del período. Aclare si ya se descontaron compromisos registrados. Puede conservar el presupuesto actual; no se inventan gastos anteriores.
steps.example: $48,000 remaining as of today; no historic spending invented.

steps.title: Añada personas y horarios
steps.text: Elija cargo, correo, idioma y acceso Personal o Super por separado. Registre días, horas y fechas. El correo verificado de su cuenta vincula su propio perfil. Las primeras tareas deben respetar las horas registradas.
steps.example: Spray Technician with Crew access, Monday–Friday 06:00–14:00.

steps.title: Confirme la base de los equipos
steps.text: Elija un modelo o añada su equipo. Confirme estado, medidor y lectura actual. Elija Desconocido cuando corresponda. Explorar el catálogo no crea historial.
steps.example: A mower has 1,245 hours today, not a guessed lifetime history.

steps.title: Cuente lo que realmente tiene
steps.text: Añada productos, semillas, materiales, repuestos, tanques e instalaciones. Confirme cantidades medidas. Los saldos iniciales no son gastos nuevos. Registre el valor de repuestos antes de emitirlos con costo; el combustible inicial requiere costo unitario.
steps.example: 12 bags counted today; unknown stock stays unconfirmed.

steps.title: Prepare el primer día
steps.text: Asigne persona, fecha, hora, duración, instrucciones y equipo opcional. Clasifique trabajo Planificado o Emergencia. Se revisan horarios, reservas, estado del equipo y restricciones de eventos.
steps.example: An operating mower and qualified worker, booked before play.

steps.title: Revise, publique y envíe por separado
steps.text: Compruebe la configuración, corrija errores y confirme la publicación. Se conserva una copia inicial verificada. Los correos quedan retenidos hasta que los libere. Guardar y salir conserva el borrador. La demostración no envía correos reales.
steps.example: Draft → review → publish → release messages → My Day.

es.deviceNote: Inicio rápido es una configuración para teléfono y computadora. Guarde cada paso para conservar el borrador privado; se mantienen los permisos normales.

examples: A mower’s meter is unreadable: choose Unknown.
There is already a budget: retain it instead of entering a second overlapping baseline.
A worker is off on Friday: move the first task rather than overriding their recorded hours.

quiz.question: Does Save & continue send welcome emails?
quiz.answer: No. Draft saves create no operational records. Publishing holds messages; release is a separate action.

quiz.question: Does one shared mower require a shared budget?
quiz.answer: No. Resource sharing choices are independent.
